tasha: deploy-bot raised an autorevert for search-infra v1.12.0 -> v1.11.5. elevated p95 and intermittent 502s on canary. change window ends 01:30 UTC. looking for manual hold.
deploy-bot: ALERT: canary search-infra p95=860ms (baseline 310ms), 502s 0.1%->1.1%. recommended rollback to v1.11.5. evidence: https://telemetry.redwood/canary/3587
ram: quick check: increased TCP retransmits on host search-04, no OOMs. might be networking flake or new connection pooling change in v1.12.0.
ops-lead: because this overlaps with scheduled DB migration at 02:00 UTC for EU customers, manual control preferred. pin for canary and rollback if operator confirms.
customer-success: two enterprise customers might see tails; please draft short blurb if we roll back.
legal: cc. file incident note if rollback executed.
tasha: assigning @ram to execute revert if needed. please suppress auto-rollback for 10m while we validate.
ram: suppressing autorevert for 10m. running smoke: `curl -s https://search.int/canary/health | jq .p95,.errors` -> p95 870ms errors 0.9%
ram: initiating rollback: `release rollback --svc search-infra --to v1.11.5 --slice 10 --strategy rolling --reason "canary tails"`
deploy-bot: ACTION: rollback initiated by ram. progress: 15% -> 50% -> 100%.
customer-success: blurb ready: "We observed a short-lived performance regression in a canary deployment and rolled back to the previous release. No customer data impacted. We'll follow up with details." sending to CSMs.
ops-lead: post-rollback metrics: p95 320ms, errors 0.15%. re-enable autoscale and routing ramp.
ram: autoscale re-enabled, monitoring 90m. saving traces for RCA.
legal: incident ticket created, no SLA breach suspected.
tasha: assigning RCA to ram and ops-lead. target writeup within 8 hours. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
